metaTitle: Simon Says — meeting notes that write themselves
metaDescription: Simon Says listens to your meeting, in the room or in Google Meet, and writes decisions and tasks live into your own Google Doc. No audio is stored. Free during the beta.
heroTitle: The meeting ends. The notes are done.
heroText: Simon Says listens to your meeting, around the table or in Google Meet, and writes decisions and tasks into your own Google Doc while you talk. By the time you stand up, everyone knows what to do.
freeLine: Free during the beta. Sign in with Google. No audio is stored.

demo.label: Example: a meeting whose notes are written while people talk
demo.caption: Made-up example. This is how the Doc fills in during the meeting.
demo.c1: Okay. Then we launch on the twelfth of March.
demo.c2: I'll write the press release by Friday, and Ella can read it.
demo.c3: And I'll book the venue tomorrow.
demo.c4: The budget lands at twenty thousand, food included.
demo.c5: By the way, the venue is booked now. The confirmation came.

phases.title: Before, during and after the meeting
phases.text: Notes are half the job. Simon Says takes care of what happens around the meeting too.
phases.beforeText: Ten minutes before a meeting in your calendar you get what matters: when you last met, decisions to remember and what is still open.
phases.duringText: Decisions and tasks appear in the Doc while you talk. Every task gets Who, When and Done when. What you type in the Doc yourself, Simon Says never touches.
phases.afterText: The summary arrives by e-mail. Everyone sees their own tasks under My tasks and ticks them off there.
phases.briefDecision: The launch is held in Linköping
phases.myTask2: Send the guest list to Maja

where.title: In the room or in Google Meet
where.text: Around a table, the laptop's microphone is enough. If the meeting is a video call, you record the tab with the call. No bot joins, and nobody else needs an account.
where.roomText: Put the laptop in the middle of the table and press Start. Pause when you want to talk without it being written down.
where.callText: Google Meet, Teams or Zoom in Chrome or Edge on a computer. You pick the tab, and Simon Says hears both you and the call.
where.bothHeard: We hear both you and the call.

foretag.title: The right people see the right meeting
foretag.text: Set the company up as a tree: management, teams and who sits where. Everyone sees their own team's meetings and what lies further down the tree. The cashier doesn't see the salary review.
foretag.point1Text: Guests from another company in the calendar become a customer. Their meetings and what is still open are gathered there.
foretag.point2Text: A short e-mail before the meeting: when you last met, what you promised and what is still open.
foretag.point3Text: If someone gets a task from a meeting they can't see, whoever held the meeting approves the text first.
foretag.pilot: Companies are being tested with a few companies right now.
foretag.treeLabel: Example: a company as a tree, and who sees a meeting in Development

foreningar.title: The board stops writing minutes
foreningar.text: Simon Says learns how you write, keeps track of your goals and gets the next meeting ready before you've gone home.
foreningar.point1Text: Import a few old minutes, and Simon Says writes the way you usually do: the same headings, in the same order.
foreningar.point2Text: Simon Says suggests goals from what keeps coming up in your meetings. You change and approve them, and they come up when you prepare the meeting.
foreningar.point3Text: The agenda takes a minute, with last week's tasks already in it. Whoever wasn't there gets the summary.
foreningar.agenda2a: Book a venue for the hackathon

privat.title: And for everything else worth remembering
privat.text: The sales call, the supervision meeting, the interview or the lecture. Record it in Private, and the summary with decisions and tasks arrives by e-mail. Sort recordings by context, such as a customer or a course. Only you see them.
privat.point2: A context per customer, course or project
privat.point3: Tasks and decisions gathered in one place
privat.mailLabel: Example: the summary that arrives by e-mail after a sales call
privat.mailSummaryText: Nordljus wants to start with two teams in April. The price is fine if onboarding is included. They decide on the contract at their management meeting next week.
privat.mailTask1: Send a quote with onboarding included, by Thursday
privat.mailTask2: Book a follow-up after their management meeting

ai.title: Your AI knows what you decided
ai.text: Connect your AI assistant to Simon Says. Ask what you agreed on the budget, which tasks you have this week, or have it add a point to the next agenda. It only sees what you can see.
ai.chatLabel: Example: a question to a connected AI assistant, with the source in the answer
ai.question: What did we decide about the launch?
ai.answer: At the planning meeting on 3 March you decided to launch on 12 March, with a budget of SEK 20,000 including food. Omar writes the press release by Friday.
ai.how: You connect under Account. You can disconnect whenever you like.

trust.title: Your meeting, your words
trust.audioText: The audio becomes text while you talk. No recording is kept, and Pause stops everything at once.
trust.docText: It lives in your own Google Drive or in the association's meeting folder. Simon Says only opens documents it created itself or that you picked.
trust.aiTitle: You see what the AI sees
trust.aiText: A connected AI can only reach what you can see yourself. Under Account you see every call and can disconnect it.
trust.gdprText: What is stored, where and for how long is in the <link>privacy information</link>.
trust.openText: The code is on <repo>GitHub</repo>. How the service is doing is on the <status>status page</status>.
trust.founder1: I sit in two associations that meet every week. After every meeting it was the same thing: somebody had to write the minutes, and the tasks were forgotten by the next time.
trust.founder2: So I built Simon Says, first for us. Now I want it to work for every meeting, not just mine. It's early, and I read everything you write to me.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Nothing right now. Simon Says is free while it's in beta. The notes live in your own Google Drive, so they're yours whatever happens.
faq.q2: What happens to the audio and what we say?
faq.a2: The audio goes straight to transcription and becomes text while you talk. No audio recording is stored. The text and the notes are kept until you delete the meeting. Who processes what is in the <link>privacy information</link>.
faq.a3: Swedish and English, even when you switch language in the middle of a sentence. The app itself is in Swedish and English.
faq.a4: No. Only the person who starts the meeting signs in with Google. Everyone else in the room is a name on the list. If they want to see their tasks, they can sign in whenever they like.
faq.a5: Start with the laptop's built-in microphone and put the laptop in the middle of the table. In a big room or a big group, a simple USB microphone helps. In a video call: use headphones, so the others are only heard once.
faq.q6: Does it work with Teams and Zoom?
faq.a6: Yes, when the call runs in the browser. Simon Says records the tab with the call in Chrome or Edge on a computer. Google Meet works straight away. Open Teams and Zoom in the browser instead of their apps. No bot joins the call.
faq.a7: Press Pause, and no audio is sent until you press Resume. Press End when you're done. A meeting also stops by itself after four hours. You can delete a meeting and disconnect your AI whenever you like.
faq.q8: Does Simon Says see the rest of my Google Drive?
faq.a8: No. Simon Says only opens documents it created itself or that you picked. We don't see the rest of your Drive.

close.title: Let your next meeting write itself
close.text: Sign in with Google, press Start and talk as usual. Getting started takes a minute.
close.signedIn: Your meetings are waiting in the app.
